necessary_conditions.text: Gamma < PSL(2,R) is a UNIFORM lattice, i.e. M := Gamma \ PSL(2,R) is COMPACT. The whole paper stays on compact quotients; finite-volume non-compact quotients (Strombergsson's setting, cited at line 155) are outside scope.
vol is the unique PSL(2,R)-invariant PROBABILITY measure on M (Haar normalized to total mass 1). Normalization matters for the zero-mean hypotheses (vol(f)=0) and for the spectral statements.

Basis U = [[0,1],[0,0]], X = [[1/2,0],[0,-1/2]], V = [[0,0],[1,0]] with [X,U]=U, [X,V]=-V, [U,V]=2X. Casimir square = -X^2 + X - UV (line 241). Flows: h_t = right mult by [[1,t],[0,1]]; phi^X_t = diag(e^{t/2}, e^{-t/2}); h^u_t = [[1,0],[t,1]] (lines 213-229). Horocycle average A_f(x,T) = (1/T) int_0^T f o h_t(x) dt for T >= 1 (lines 236-238).

mu real eigenvalue of square; nu in R_{>=0} union i R_{>0} with (1 - nu^2)/4 = mu. Regimes: mu > 1/4 (nu purely imaginary, principal), mu = 1/4 (nu = 0, double root -1/2), 0 < mu < 1/4 (nu in (0,1), complementary), mu = 0, mu < 0 (discrete, mu = -n^2+n, n >= 1 integer, lines 798-801).
Theorem 1: f in C^2(M) AND a Casimir eigenfunction (square f = mu f). The eigenfunction hypothesis is essential; Theorem 1 is not a statement about general C^2 functions.

Theorem 2: f in W^6(M) only, no eigenfunction hypothesis; the spectral decomposition replaces it. W^r is defined at lines 356-361 as maximal domain of (Id+Delta)^{r/2} with inner product <(Id+Delta)^r f, g> (this is a 2r-order form; the convention must be preserved when quoting the W^6 threshold).
W^4(M) subset C^2(M) with ||f||_{C^2} <= C_emb ||f||_{W^4}; since dim M = 3 any r > 7/2 would do. The paper keeps r = 4 and r = 6 throughout.

The uniform summability is over ALL mu in Spec(square) cap R_{>0}, with tilde C_M = max{|nu|^{-1}, |1-nu|^{-1}} over sigma_comp union sigma_princ finite because the spectrum is discrete and bounded away from the endpoints except possibly at 1/4 (where eps_0 handles it).

Theorem 4 (spatial DLT): f in W^6 real-valued with vol(f) = 0; mu_f := min{mu in Spec(square) cap R_{>0} : D^-_mu f not identically 0} is assumed FINITE, and D^-_{mu_f} f is non-zero by construction (this is what makes the limit law non-Dirac and compactly supported, lines 478-479).

Theorem 5 / appendix Theorem 20: f in W^6 real, vol(f) = 0; hypothesis (a) 1/4 not in Spec(square) and D^pm_mu f identically 0 for all positive mu, OR hypothesis (b) all positive-parameter components are measurable coboundaries; and f is NOT a measurable coboundary for the horocycle flow.

The equivalence used in the appendix is: f not a measurable coboundary for U implies Vf_0 not a measurable coboundary for X (Lemma 18 last claim, argued as in Remark 12 using Livsic, minimality of h_t, Gottschalk-Hedlund). It is not asserted as an iff.

quantifiers_and_regularity.text: Theorem 1 statements hold 'for all x in M and T >= 1', with sup-norm bounds on the coefficients; these are POINTWISE-IN-x identities with uniform constants, not a.e. statements.
x_T abbreviates phi^X_{log T}(x); the coefficients are evaluated at the geodesic-shifted point, so the expansion is not a function of x alone.

Complementary series: D^+ f has exponent (1-nu)/2, D^- f has exponent (1+nu)/2. Principal series: both exponent 1/2. mu = 1/4: D^+ only 1/2 - eps for EVERY eps > 0 (no fixed exponent), D^- exactly 1/2. Theorem 2 restates these as (1 -/+ Re nu)/2 with the 1/4 exception (line 398).

Theorem 2 sums over the whole spectrum with the same pointwise-in-x expansion; the sums are over sigma_comp, sigma_princ and the optional 1/4 term. Summability of the sup-norms is what makes the displayed infinite sum meaningful.
Convergence is IN DISTRIBUTION for t ~ U_[0,T] (uniform on the time interval), with x FIXED deterministic. It is not almost-sure, not uniform in x, and not a statement about a random base point.

Theorem 4 is a QUANTITATIVE weak-convergence statement measured in the Levy-Prokhorov distance d_LP, with x ~ vol. For mu_f > 1/4 the target D(f,T) is itself T-dependent ('moving target'); no genuine limit law is claimed in that regime.
Lemma 18: the error E(x,T) is bounded by C_M ||f||_{W^4} UNIFORMLY in x and T; the leading term is the difference of two geodesic integrals over [0, log T].

normalization_boundaries.text: A_f carries the 1/T factor; the ergodic INTEGRAL int_0^T f o h_t dt = T A_f. The existing 2150 statement (T^{-(1+nu)/2}, T^{-(1-nu)/2}) is in the A_f normalization; do not silently switch to integrals.
Spatial DLT renormalizations: T^{-(1+nu_f)/2} int_0^T f o h_t dt if mu_f != 1/4; (T^{1/2} log T)^{-1} int_0^T f o h_t dt if mu_f = 1/4.
Temporal normalization is sqrt(log T) with the explicit centering -int_0^{log T} Vf_0 o phi^X_s(x) ds; the centering is a real number depending on x, not a constant.
The -UV term (not -2UV or -VU/2) fixes the spectral parameter relation; a different Casimir normalization shifts mu by constants and changes all exponents of T.

Delta = -(X^2+Y^2+Theta^2) = square - 2 Theta^2; the W^r norm and the Theta-eigenfunction splitting in Lemma 14 depend on this exact relation and on Theta eigenvalues k in Z (positive mu) or in n + Z_{>=0} (discrete series).

core_recount_boundaries.text: Already counted in old 2150/H2 and NOT to be recounted anywhere: (1) conversion of the Casimir equation into the forced ODE J'' + J' + mu J = e^{-t} G(t) (Proposition 8) with the uniform bound |G| <= 2||f||_{C^2}; (2) the global coefficient integrals and the tracking of the two complementary-series exponents with the inverse-time tail estimate; (3) the anisotropic geodesic expansion |G(y,xi) - G(x,xi)| <= 6||f||_{C^2} min{1, r e^xi} plus the elementary weighted integral bound, giving the exact Holder exponents; (4) the auxiliary average bounds eq:aux_thm_1_princ / eq:aux_thm_1_comp.

We used as external inputs and did not count: Weyl's law (Lemma 13), the Sobolev embedding constant C_emb, Flaminio–Forni's classification/cohomological results, Ratner's CLT for geodesic integrals and its sigma, Eagleson's theorem, Dolgopyat–Sarig Th. 5.1, Gottschalk–Hedlund, Livsic, Barut–Raczka for the possible non-positive Casimir eigenvalues.

Theorem 1(i),(ii),(iv),(v) and Lemma 11 are same-core parameter variants of the adopted branch (iii): the differential equation, the coefficient construction and the geodesic-expansion exponent argument are the same; different root multiplicities, oscillatory presentation or endpoint cases do not constitute an independent construction.
Theorem 4 and Lemma 18 (and Remark 16) are direct applications/adaptations of Theorem 2; Proposition 3 is an explicit computation on the already-constructed coefficients. Not counted separately.

The appendix (lines 1184-1387) is authored by Emilio Corso. Its Theorem 20 / Lemma 21 / Proposition 22 must not be merged into or attributed to the 2150 main-text record, even though it reuses the main text's Theorem 2 through Lemma 18.
